act: Indian Stamp Act, 1899, Schedule I Art. 23A (as applicable to the NCT of Delhi)

source.ref: Indian Stamp Act, 1899, Sch. I Art. 23A (ins. Act 48 of 2001, w.e.f. 24-9-2001)
source.quoted_text: Central Sch. I Art. 23A (both columns, from the Delhi-Revenue-hosted Act text): 'CONVEYANCE IN THE NATURE OF PART PERFORMANCE — Contracts for the transfer of immovable property in the nature of part performance in any union territory under section 53A of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882' — 'Ninety per cent of the duty as a Conveyance (No. 23)'. Applies to an agreement to sell WHERE POSSESSION IS DELIVERED (s.53A part performance). Transfer duty: a 'contract for transfer of immovable property' is in the DMC s.147 list with base 90% of consideration (founder Q1).

notes_for_reviewer: CONFIDENCE: MEDIUM-HIGH for the stamp leg (Art 23A text is clean: 90% of conveyance duty; encoded as cross_ref scale 0.9 on consideration). Art 23A speaks of 'any union territory' — Delhi (NCT) treatment as UT for this article is settled practice but note it. Central Sch I fn: duty paid under 23A is excluded when computing duty on the completing conveyance (SET-OFF) — the set-off itself is a Flow-D/memo feature, not a charge change; flagged for M3. ROUTE VIA QUESTIONNAIRE: possession delivered → this rule; no possession → DL-ART5c-agreement-to-sell (Rs 50).

act: Indian Stamp Act, 1899 (as applicable to Delhi), Schedule I-A

source.ref: Indian Stamp Act, 1899, Sch. I-A Art. 5(c) (Delhi)
source.quoted_text: Sch I-A Art. 5 (both columns): 'AGREEMENT OR MEMORANDUM OF AN AGREEMENT ... (c) If not otherwise provided for — Fifty rupees.' An agreement to sell immovable property WITHOUT delivery of possession is not separately provided for in Sch I-A and is stamped as an Art 5(c) agreement (Rs 50). (Where possession is delivered it is instead chargeable as a conveyance in part performance under Art 23A — see DL-ART23A-ats-part-performance.)

notes_for_reviewer: CONFIDENCE: MEDIUM. The possession fork (Rs 50 vs 90%-of-conveyance + transfer duty) is enormous and classification-sensitive — MUST be routed by the questionnaire, never defaulted. NOTE the Sch I-A women-reduction text mentions 'Agreement to sale' alongside conveyance — if Delhi practice charges ad valorem duty on certain no-possession ATS variants, this Rs 50 reading is too generous; founder to confirm registrar practice.
